title: Async context shim for SDKs and frameworks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Distributed traces and request-level metrics are intermittently losing trace/context information across asynchronous boundaries in our SDKs and framework middleware. Root causes observed in recent incidents: Node async_hooks interactions with third-party promise libraries, Python asyncio tasks dropping contextvars in threadpool work, and mismatch between in-memory context and header propagation at gateway boundaries. This leads to partial traces, scattered spans, and incorrect error attribution in dashboards.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight 'async-context-shim' library + a set of framework adapters that: (1) provide a consistent context carrier API for SDKs (startSpan, getContext, runWithContext, bindHandler), (2) bridge runtime-specific mechanisms (Node async_hooks, Python contextvars, Go context.Context, Ruby Fiber-local) behind a unified surface, (3) include middleware adapters (Express/Koa, FastAPI/Starlette, gRPC interceptors) that automatically propagate trace id, sampling decision, and baggage across inbound/outbound requests, and (4) add a small opt-in auto-instrumentation hook for popular HTTP clients and RPC libs. The shim will prefer low-overhead in-memory carriers but fall back to header-based propagation for cross-process calls. Sampling decisions must be made available to downstream services without forcing span allocation (deferred-span pattern).

Design notes: keep public API minimal to avoid adoption friction; default to W3C traceparent and baggage headers; allow platform-configurable sampling header (x-rd-sample) for legacy customers; expose a diagnostic mode that logs context deltas for staging to help instrument poorly-behaved libraries.

Risks & trade-offs: supporting many language runtimes adds maintenance cost; to mitigate, start with Node and Python (highest customer impact) then converge on a small, well-documented Go adapter. Deferred span allocation reduces overhead but complicates latency attribution for short-lived requests — acceptability gated by perf benchmarks.
acceptance_criteria: A published npm package @redwood/async-context-shim with documented API and semantic versioning
Express and Koa middleware implemented and landing PRs merged
FastAPI/Starlette and gRPC interceptor for Python implemented and tested
End-to-end staging test: a two-service request preserves trace id and sampling decision across async boundaries (trace visible in Jaeger/Zipkin)
Automated integration test asserting traceparent header propagation for HTTP and gRPC
Performance: overhead measured <1% p50 and <5% p99 on synthetic request workload compared to baseline (no shim) in CI benchmarks
Docs: migration guide, API reference, troubleshooting section (diagnostic logs) published in Confluence and linked from SDK README
Canary rollout plan documented and approved by SRE and Product
tasks: Write design RFC and run 1:1 review with SRE and PM (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Async+Context+Shim+RFC)
Prototype shim for Node (use async_hooks + native AsyncLocalStorage fallback) and validate with Express app
Prototype shim for Python (contextvars + threadpool adapter) and validate with FastAPI
Implement middleware adapters for Express/Koa and FastAPI/Starlette
Add gRPC interceptors for Python and Node (where applicable)
Create integration tests that spawn two services and assert trace continuity
Benchmark perf impact in small cluster; capture p50/p95/p99 and memory overhead
Write SDK integration guide and update SDK CHANGELOGs
Open security review ticket and address crypto/KMS implications for baggage/encryption
